questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for you to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other road users what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and hazards on the road. Your lane position should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding. When a lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: To increase your line of sight when preparing to pass another vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass another vehicle on its left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases your risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: To stop quickly, it is best to:

options.text: Slow the engine and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks that cross at an angle, ride straight across them within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could end up in another lane of traffic.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see the wearer.
Can be distracting.
Do not improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see the wearer.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other road users see you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Do not need space cushions.
Should increase their space cushions.
Should cut their usual space cushions in half.
Should keep an adequate space cushion around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep an adequate space cushion around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, ride close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Cannot tip over.
Can tip over if turning too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not carry any items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if the turn is too sharp or the speed is too fast for the corner.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Brake gradually.
Speed up.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Shift your weight forward and down. Leave the road when it is safe. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed steady to improve grip.
Ignore the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: The best choice is to avoid slippery roads entirely. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and ride as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle should:

options.text: Allow you to touch the ground with your feet while seated.
Have a seat level with your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely.
Hold the handgrips firmly.
Use high throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This helps you maintain control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. This includes wet pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. Staying left gives you more space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
Follow other drivers closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready for changes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do when turning?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through turns by turning only your head and eyes. Press your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. You are more likely to notice a sudden change in how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle operators and other drivers have the most conflict?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcyclists and other drivers have the most conflicts. Riders should be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Not ride during the day.
Look for safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To reduce your risk of a crash, make yourself visible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle but still fail to notice it. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: Before getting on your motorcycle, your pre-ride check should include everything except:

options.text: A tire check.
A taillight test.
A headlight test.
A paint check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A paint check.
questions.explanation: A pre-ride check should include tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a full pre-ride check before every ride.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if you use it properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on riding conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position or position to avoid. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning a curve usually happens because:

options.text: You are taking the turn too fast.
The lanes are too narrow.
You do not know how to steer.
The lanes are too wide.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve at a speed that is too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: If you are riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Stay in a position that makes you visible to the driver.
Always ride in the far left part of the lane.
Not worry about your position.
Always ride in the far right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position that makes you visible to the driver.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center part of your lane. This position is most likely to be visible in the car's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Speed up before downshifting safely.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes so drivers behind you know you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down enough to shift safely. Downshifting at high speed can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, use the brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Allow you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position improves safety. It keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid road hazards and wind from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.
